messages.subject: HR in non-habitable areas
parts:
Hi Christen,
I work with terrestrial species (dogs), which sometimes go the sea (but exceptionally), and not far away. Only one individual moves constantly in the sea, but does not move more than 100 m away from the coast.
Some of my individuals have a very large HR, and it covers marine areas that they can not use (water is very cold here). I think that cutting the HR is an option, but I haven't found any information about it. If you have any references could you share it please?
So, I wanted to ask you what would you do if the HR is established in areas where the species cannot live? What do you think about this?

thanks!

Best
Lorena
